ctx_execute: Runs code in a sandboxed subprocess in the project directory and returns only what the code prints. Languages: shell, powershell, javascript, typescript, python, and other runtimes found on PATH. Use it when output may be long, for example tests, builds, logs, git history or API responses, and print just the lines or numbers you need. Set `file` to a local path to work on that file without reading it into the conversation; the code gets the path in the CTX_FILE environment variable. Set `intent` to a short phrase when output may be large: the matching sections come back and the full output is indexed for ctx_search. Stops after `timeoutMs` (default 120000) and kills the whole process tree.
ctx_batch: Runs several shell commands, then answers several search queries over their combined output, in one call. Use it to collect facts from more than one command at once, for example test results plus recent commits, when you need specific answers rather than the full text. Returns the matching sections and a one-line footer.
ctx_index: Stores content so it can be searched later: a local file or folder (nested .gitignore files are respected), raw text, or a URL, which is fetched and converted to Markdown. Use it for documentation or large files you will query more than once, then use ctx_search instead of reading the content again. Returns the source label and how many chunks were stored.
ctx_search: Searches content stored with ctx_index and earlier sandbox output in this project. Pass several queries in one call. By default it searches the current worktree; set `scope` to `project` for all worktrees or `session` for this session only. Results from the current session rank first, and every hit names its source. When nothing matches, the reply states the scope and how many sources are indexed.
ctx_resume: Returns a summary of up to 2 KB for this session: the last task and user request, files changed, open errors, decisions, and search terms for ctx_search. Use it after the conversation was compacted or resumed, before you repeat earlier work.
ctx_stats: Reports how many bytes context-mode kept out of the conversation in this session and in this project, per agent. Use it when the user asks what context-mode saved.
ctx_purge: Deletes stored data: one session, one indexed source, or everything stored for this project. This cannot be undone. Use it only when the user asks to forget or reset data.
